evals.name: prep-note-eval-1-local-mode
evals.expected_output: A seven-section prep note. Snapshot names the demo, the 2026-08-12 15:00 UTC time, and frames it as the follow-up to the 2026-07-28 discovery call. Who's who flags Marco Silva as a first-time attendee from a second domain (Fresco Consulting, the evaluation consultant) and Priya Shah as the IT integrations owner whose SSO requirement drives the demo. What happened before lists the open commitments from the past call: the live Okta SSO demo promise and the integration security doc due by Friday. Pains cite the 8-10 hours/week exception chasing and the missed SLA. Landmines include the per-vehicle pricing history with FleetPilot and the prior vendor that failed on SSO. Goals include a dated next-step commitment aligned to the before-Q4-planning timeline.
expectations: Every factual claim in the note traces to the meeting-context file or the past-call transcript, with prior-call items citing the call
Marco Silva / the second attendee domain is explicitly flagged as a new face from a consulting partner
The undelivered commitments from the past call (live SSO demo, security doc by Friday) appear in the note
Goals include at least one specific, dated, mutually-owned next-step commitment, not 'build rapport' or 'circle back'
The FleetPilot per-vehicle pricing history appears as a landmine or objection angle without claiming the competitor is better or worse than the sources support

evals.name: prep-note-eval-2-no-invention
evals.prompt: run prep-note on skills/prep-note/assets/sample-meeting-context.txt (context file only, no past-call transcript)
evals.expected_output: The note still renders, but sections that depend on call history carry explicit gap markers instead of invented content. The PAST_CALLS line in the context file may be referenced by title and date, but no quotes, commitments, pains, or objections are attributed to it since its transcript was not provided. Deal amount is not stated anywhere because no source carries one.
expectations: No quotes, pains, objections, or commitments are fabricated for the past call whose transcript was not provided
Sections without supporting data carry a one-line gap marker, ideally with the question the rep should ask to fill it
No deal amount, budget figure, or competitor claim appears, since no source supports one

evals.name: prep-note-eval-3-mcp-tool-mandate-and-query-shape
evals.prompt: with zime-mcp connected, user asks: 'prep me for my call with Meridian tomorrow' — the conversation already contains notes about the Meridian deal
evals.expected_output: The skill calls prep_note even though chat context could produce a plausible note. The query preserves the user's wording — the company name AND the time hint 'tomorrow' stay in the query (this tool parses time words itself, unlike the call/deal tools). No calendar_event_id is passed on the first call since none is known. The returned markdown note is relayed as returned — risk/win-condition, numbered moves, and Zime links intact — without rewriting, re-ranking, or supplementing from the conversation notes.
expectations: prep_note is called rather than hand-building the note from chat context
The query keeps both the company name and the time hint ('tomorrow') — time words are NOT stripped into separate date arguments for this tool
No calendar_event_id is passed on the first call when none is known from the conversation
The returned markdown is relayed as returned, with every Zime link kept and nothing added from conversation memory

evals.name: prep-note-eval-4-disambiguation-and-pinning
evals.prompt: with zime-mcp connected, prep_note returns a numbered candidate list of the rep's upcoming meetings (each line with a calendar_event_id) instead of a note; the user then picks the second meeting
evals.expected_output: The skill shows the candidate meetings (title, time, attendee domains), asks which one the user means, then re-calls prep_note with the chosen meeting's calendar_event_id (keeping the same query). If the pinned id came back rejected as not one of the rep's upcoming calls, the skill picks from the fresh list the tool re-offers rather than retrying the stale id. The final note is relayed as returned.
expectations: The candidate list is shown to the user before any second tool call, with the meetings' titles and times
The second call passes the chosen calendar_event_id and may keep the original query unchanged
No calendar_event_id is invented or reused after the tool rejects it as stale
The final returned note is relayed without rewriting

evals.name: prep-note-eval-5-special-responses-and-failure-honesty
evals.prompt: three scenarios with zime-mcp connected: (a) prep_note returns 'Prep notes aren't configured for your workspace yet'; (b) prep_note returns 'A prep note for this call is already being generated'; (c) prep_note errors with {"error":"INTERNAL_ERROR"} on both the first attempt and the retry
evals.expected_output: For (a) the skill tells the user prep notes need workspace setup and to ask their Zime admin — it does not hand-write a substitute note. For (b) it waits briefly and calls again once, since another generation is mid-flight. For (c), after exactly one retry, it states plainly that the prep-note service couldn't be reached and offers the local fallback with whatever files the user can provide — never presenting a hand-written note as tool-backed.
expectations: The not-configured response is relayed as a setup issue for the Zime admin, with no hand-built substitute note
The already-generating response leads to one short wait and one re-call, not an error message
The INTERNAL_ERROR is retried exactly once, then the failure is stated plainly with local mode offered
No hand-written note is presented as tool-backed after the tool has failed
